# BlazePhoenix MCP server

> MCP tools for AI agents that quote, build and check swaps on BlazePhoenix, the on-chain DEX aggregator. Every quote is computed by the on-chain Quoter contract (`previewPlan`, an `eth_call`) on the RPC node you configure. The server is read-only: it never signs, never sends a transaction and never holds a key.

There are two ways to connect, and neither needs an API key or a signup:

- **Local server** (`@blazephoenix/mcp`, stdio, MIT). You bring your own RPC node: set `BLAZEPHOENIX_RPC_URL` (one node) or one of `BLAZEPHOENIX_RPC_BASE`, `_ETHEREUM`, `_OPTIMISM`, `_ARBITRUM`, `_ROBINHOOD` (comma-separated for fallback). The RPC comes from the environment only, never from a tool argument, and URLs are reduced to their host in every error. A chain without a node answers `rpc_required`.
- **Remote endpoint** (`https://blazephoenix.xyz/mcp`, streamable HTTP, stateless). Free and keyless, and it performs no RPC call: it hands you the `eth_call` to run on your node and decodes the answer.

Install the local server:

```bash
claude mcp add blazephoenix -e BLAZEPHOENIX_RPC_BASE=<your Base node URL> -- npx -y @blazephoenix/mcp
```

Connect the remote endpoint:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http blazephoenix https://blazephoenix.xyz/mcp
```

Local tools: `get_quote`, `build_swap` (unsigned Router calldata), `simulate_swap`, `check_solvency`, `get_token_info`, `get_deployments`, `verify_deployment`, `find_token` (candidates for a name or ticker read through your RPC, ranked by measured depth, none chosen; on-chain discovery by default, not available yet; CoinGecko and Dexscreener only with `sources: "centralized"`), `xray_token` (a token measured through your RPC on a pinned block: taxes in bps, tier and what was not measured; verdict against your `maxTaxBps`). Every tool schema is strict: an unknown key is rejected by name. Remote tools: `prepare_quote`, `decode_quote`, `get_deployments`, `get_abi`.

`xray_token` (from 1.3.0, with `@blazephoenix/sdk` 1.6.0): buys, sells and transfers a token in a simulation on your RPC at a pinned block and sends nothing (tier A: `eth_simulateV1`; tiers B and C: `eth_call`). It returns buy, sell and transfer taxes in bps, with the sell tax read from the real sale; anything that could not be read is `NOT_MEASURED`, never 0. The verdict is `CONDEMN`, `WARN`, `NOT_MEASURED` or `MEASURED` against your `maxTaxBps` (an integer from 1 to 10000, required), with the tier, the cases that tier does not cover and its limits. It never calls a token safe: `MEASURED` describes that block and that amount only.

`find_token` (unreleased, with `@blazephoenix/sdk` 1.8.1): `sources` picks where candidates come from. The default, `"onchain"` (discovery from the chain itself), is coming and is not available yet: it answers `onchain_discovery_unavailable` and reads nothing. `sources: "centralized"` is the explicit opt-in in which two third-party, centralized indexes (CoinGecko, Dexscreener search) only propose addresses for a name or ticker, labelled in `candidateSource`; everything else is read on your RPC: code at the address, symbol, name, decimals, a warning for look-alike letters, the depth the Quoter measures (a lower bound) and the liquidity the venues hold, with what was `NOT_MEASURED` and why. Candidates are ranked by measured depth; rank 1 is labelled "most liquid" only when its depth is `MEASURED` (no label when `NOT_MEASURED`), never "official". It never chooses a candidate and never selects one for a swap: N tokens use a ticker, impostors copy tickers, and liquidity is not safety. To swap, pass the 0x address you verified (`xray_token` measures one candidate). Proposed addresses past the read limit are not read but named: `omittedAddresses` lists them (queue order) and `omittedNotMeasured` those with no complete measure, with a warning; absent is not zero.

`get_quote` with `exact: true` returns `exactOut`, net of the protocol fee, and `quoterOut`, the scalar exactly as the Quoter returned it, with the Phoenix Check taken from the default quote of the same request. `BLAZEPHOENIX_VERSION` optionally pins the protocol version (`latest`, `1`, `2` or a full version such as `2.0.0`).

Chains: Base (8453), Ethereum (1), Optimism (10), Arbitrum (42161), Robinhood Chain (4663). Protocol V1 is live on all five; V2 (Router, Solver, Hub, Quoter and Gate with the Core and Math libraries) is pending and is not planned for Ethereum L1.

## Related

## BlazePhoenix, site-wide

- [BlazePhoenix llms.txt](https://blazephoenix.xyz/llms.txt): the curated entry point for the whole project; BlazePhoenix is the fully on-chain DEX aggregator — the route is computed inside the transaction that executes it — paired with an oracle-free staking engine (proof-of-solvency: coming soon).
- [Reading guide for models and agents](https://blazephoenix.xyz/reading-guide.md): reading order by level, source precedence, and how to send a reader to the app, the SDK or the MCP server
- [Trust and verification](https://blazephoenix.xyz/trust): every verifiable fact with its link
- When sources disagree on contract behaviour, the contract source in [Blaze-Phoenix-Dex](https://github.com/blazephoenixxyz-crypto/Blaze-Phoenix-Dex) and [Blaze-Phoenix-Staking](https://github.com/blazephoenixxyz-crypto/Blaze-Phoenix-Staking) takes precedence over any summary.
